approvedEdges.reason: Same 4th Dynasty king with matching prenomen (Cha'ef-rê = kha.ef ra) and corroborating name correspondence (Chephren/Khafre).
Same 4th Dynasty king: prenomen Cha'ef-rê (Beckerath) matches Khaf Ra (pharaoh_se), and display names Chephren/Khafra are Greek/Egyptian forms of the same ruler.
Both records share the same prenomen (Men-kau-rê), same Dynasty 4, and their display names (Mykerinos/Menkaure/Mycerinus) are well-known variant transliterations of the same 4th Dynasty king.
Same dynasty 4 king with matching prenomen Men-kaw-rê/Men kau Ra and known name variants (Mykerinos/Menkaure) of the same Fourth Dynasty pyramid builder.
Same dynasty 6 king with matching prenomen Merenre and matching nomen Nemtiemsaf; reign-date differences reflect scholarly disagreement, not distinct identities.

Same dynasty, matching prenomen (Nebhepetre) with consistent transliteration differences, identical nomen (Mentuhotep II), and overlapping reign windows confirm the same well-known 11th-Dynasty unifier king.
Both records place the king in Dynasty 11 with prenomen Sankhkara and matching Horus name Sankhtawy; reign window and nomen also agree, identifying Mentuhotep III.
Same dynasty 11, matching prenomen Sankhkare, matching nomen Mentuhotep, and consistent identity as Mentuhotep III; reign-date differences are within normal cross-source variation.
Same dynasty 11, same nomen (Mentuhotep IV), same distinctive prenomen (Nebtawyre), and same 7-year reign length despite date-offset from differing chronology frameworks.
Same dynasty 12, same prenomen Khakheperre (unique to this king), and matching regnal number II; name variants are standard transliterations of the same king.
Same dynasty 12, prenomen Khakaure matches, and Sesostris/Senwosret are Greek and Egyptian forms of the same nomen for this king.
Both records share dynasty 12, the prenomen Khakaure (variant transliterations), and regnal numeral III; reign-date divergence reflects differing chronological schemes, not distinct kings.
Same 12th Dynasty king: matching nomen (Amenemhat/Ammenemes III) and prenomen (Ni-maat-rê); reign-date divergence reflects standard scholarly chronological disagreement.
Same dynasty 12, prenomen Maa-kheru-rê, and nomen Amenemhat/Ammenemes IV corroborate identity.

Same dynasty, matching prenomen Maa-kheru-Ra, and nomen Amenemhat/Ammenemes are variant transliterations of the same king; the ~35-year date offset reflects differing chronological frameworks for the 12th Dynasty.
Same queen of Dynasty 12 with matching prenomen Ka-sobek-rê and nomen variants of Sobekneferu; all contextual elements align.
Same Dynasty 15 Hyksos king: matching prenomen variants Aqenenre and Auserre, with nomen Apophis/Apepi corroborating identity.
Same 15th Dynasty Hyksos king: nomen Apophis/Apopi matches, and two prenomen variants (Aqenenre, Aweserre) are shared across both records.
Same king Ahmose I, founder of the 18th Dynasty: nomen variants (Amosis/Iah-mesu) and prenomen Neb-pehti-rê match; reign-date divergence reflects different chronological schemes.
Same king: Dynasty 18, Amenhotep I, prenomen Djeser-ka-rê matches across both sources, with consistent nomen and dynasty context.
Same dynasty, same prenomen Djeser-ka-rê/Djoser-ka-Ra, same nomen Amenhotep/Amenophis, consistent identity for 18th Dynasty king Amenhotep I.
Same dynasty 18, prenomen A-kheper-en-rê matches, and nomina Tuthmosis/Thutmose II agree; records denote the same king.
Same dynasty 18, same prenomen Maat-ka-rê, and same nomen Hatshepsut together securely identify the famous female pharaoh Hatshepsut.
Same dynasty 18, identical prenomen Neferkheperure-waenre, matching nomen Amenhotep IV, overlapping reign dates, and the Akhenaten name change confirm this is the same well-documented king.
Both records share prenomen Ankhkheperure, dynasty 18, nomen Smenkhkara, and overlapping reign dates (~1337–1333 BCE), providing corroboration beyond display-name alone.
Same dynasty 18, prenomen Kheperkheperure Irimaat matches in both records, and nomen Aja/Ay/Iy corresponds; records denote Tutankhamun's successor Ay.
Same 18th Dynasty king: prenomen Kheperkheperure matches, reign windows overlap (~1323–1319 BCE), and nomina Aja/Ay are variant transcriptions of the same ruler.
Same dynasty, same reign window, matching prenomen Djeser-cheprurê/Djoser-kheperu-Ra, and matching nomen Horemheb/Har-em-hab; all context corroborates identity.
Same dynasty (19), prenomen (Men-pehty-rê), nomen (Ramessu), and overlapping reign window (~1292–1290/1291 BCE) corroborate identity.
